audit.summary: Two local concerns are supported: Appendix A.14's step-count summaries cannot describe one common set of trials under their stated all/success/failure partition, and the pinned released matching utility can accept answers with incorrect numeric associations. Neither check establishes that the published success rates are wrong. The source release is not proven identical to the experimental evaluator, so the historical score impact remains Needs Evidence. The architecture and synthetic-data strategy were inspected without establishing a separate core invalidity.
limitations: P1 — The reported step-count breakdown violates the weighted-mean identity — Counterevidence: Rendered and visually inspected the exact original PDF p.43; table numerals are genuine and not a text-extraction error. Separately averaging conditional means across runs with unequal success counts, using different populations, or an undisclosed step-count convention could explain different numbers, but none is stated for this table. Such a reading would itself require relabeling the reported common breakdown and supplying denominators. Success counts themselves are mutually consistent (16,16,17,25,12,3 sum to 89); therefore this does not show the 53.94% main success rate is wrong.

P2 — Released exact matching loses the association between keys and numeric values — Counterevidence: Order-insensitive matching can be correct for an unordered collection, but here the order establishes which month has which count; sorting the complete key-value pairs is different from erasing their internal bindings. Unicode or punctuation normalization cannot justify swapping values. Released run scripts call a previous_rounds evaluator, but import it from evaluation_harness; the inspected repository file is delivered under plan_and_act. This path mapping and the actual historical runtime are not established. The commit was observed in 2026 and no statement equates it to the publication-time revision. Therefore no number of false positives in published experiments, and no lowered benchmark score, has been established.

Limitations: The paper explicitly calls the targeted-augmentation set a held-out validation set (§4.3 p.7; A.10 p.31). The error-analysis tool can consume a generic test_set_path, but this is not proof of test leakage; no leakage finding is made. Task-level split identities and synthetic-data overlap were not available in the inspected bounded snapshot.
Limitations: Published benchmark numbers, per-task raw logs, judge agreement and provenance of the experimental evaluator were not reproduced.
Limitations: Source snapshot alone does not establish publication-time code equivalence. Later revisions/errata outside the staged sources were not searched.

proposition.claim:
Section 5.1, p.7, defines binary complete-task success; Appendix A.14, Figure 4, p.43, reports number of tasks, average steps over all tasks, over successful tasks and over failures, plus success rate, for a common task breakdown. Overall: N=165, all=11.12, successful=7.52, failed=13.43, success rate=53.9%.

Section 5.1, p.7, evaluates complete task success with binary success/failure. The pinned repository exposes an exact_match utility whose implementation returns equality of alphanumeric token Counters after simple normalized-string variants fail (utils.py lines 1037-1051). The string evaluator calls this utility (previous_rounds_evaluators.py lines 136-137,174-175); its must_include rule calls a token-set-subset utility (utils.py lines 1011-1025; evaluator lines 195-201).
proposition.domain: Completed report for I25-43522; exact inspected scope and limitations are retained in the report and coverage ledger.
assumptions: All/Success/Fail columns summarize the same finite trial population, with success and failure exhaustive and disjoint, as their labels and the binary success definition indicate.
Means are ordinary task means and displayed decimal means round to 0.01; displayed success percentages round to 0.1 percentage point.
The 165 overall tasks are the sum of the six website rows; 53.9% is compatible with exactly 89 successful tasks at that denominator.
Both reference and proposed answer are ordinary ASCII strings, with no diacritics, unusual spaces, dash/slash/dot separators or control characters, so canonicalize leaves them unchanged.
Choose a task asking for a mapping from month IDs to counts; the paper itself illustrates this output form in Appendix A.5.2, pp.19-21.
For the finite counterexample, evaluate the exact_match branch on a reference and proposed answer, without claiming the actual benchmark uses this specific configuration or recorded erroneous answer.
This is static source reasoning plus an independently written token arithmetic check; the author modules, dependencies and benchmark were not executed.

repair.content:
Do not choose one column to overwrite based solely on this identity. Recompute all three means and denominators from the same per-task trace records, or explicitly describe distinct weighting/populations if intentional. The displayed other columns imply an overall all-mean of approximately 10.24 only conditionally; this is an arithmetic implication, not a verified replacement for the empirical table.

For a fixed month:count output schema, parse into a mapping and compare the full key-value relation (after allowed canonicalization). This restores the exhibited pairing requirement. It is not a universal replacement for all benchmark string or fuzzy matching, and no revised benchmark implementation is certified.
